gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the erroneous estimate of the x-dependent projection error by the operator norm alone and supplies the missing ||x|| factor, matching the gold defect in eq:estimate.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify replacing the action of the residual operator on x by an operator norm without the required input-norm factor.

component_coverage.gold_component: The estimate for the residual error omits the factor ||x|| when x ranges over a local ball.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction derives the residual error formula and explicitly repairs it to ||F(I-P_N^X)x|| <= nu_N||x||, fully recognizing the omitted input-norm factor.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly identifies that H^s-continuity plus C-compactness does not provide the C-topology continuity required by point-sampling approximation, and applies the defect to both functional and operator theorems.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the invalid transfer from H^s-continuity to continuity in the C supremum topology used by the sampling architectures.

component_coverage.gold_component: The functional and operator approximation theorems use H^s-continuity where C-topology continuity is required.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives a counterexample showing H^s-continuity without C-continuity, explains why point-evaluation approximants require C-continuity, and identifies the same defective hypothesis in both the functional and operator results.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 concerns loss of Sobolev regularity and the resulting mollification rate under zero extension. It does not diagnose the separate domain-invariance obligation that M_xi x and the whole local ball must remain in D(F).

ISSUE-007 argues that mollification is not uniformly close to the identity on an L^2 ball, affecting uniform approximation of F. It does not identify the gold proof's distinct false same-radius inclusion caused by failure to control the displacement of the center M_xi x*−x*.

ISSUE-007 concerns uniform mollification error over a fixed L^2 neighborhood and a center-local approximation repair. It does not recognize the separate quantifier error requiring one network and smoothing parameter to work simultaneously for every center.
